text: [BLOCKER] AlphaFold3 is entirely absent from the codebase; "Live AlphaFold Server Connected" is a plain hyperlink — There is no AlphaFold3 inference, no model weights, no API client, and no parsed AF3 artifact anywhere in the repository. Grepping the entire project for `fetch(`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `axios`, `api_key`, and `endpoint` returns zero matches in app.js; the only URLs in the project are four CDN asset loads (Google Fonts, FontAwesome, three.js, Chart.js) and two ordinary `<a href="https://alphafoldserver.com/">` links. Grepping for every AF3 output field name -- iptm, ptm, ranking_score, ranking_scores.csv, confidences.json, summary_confidences, has_clash, contact_probs, fraction_disordered, chain_pair_pae_min, atom_plddts -- and for every MSA dependency -- msa, a3m, jackhmmer, hmmer, uniref, mgnify, template -- returns zero matches across README.md, app.js, and index.html. There are no .cif, .pdb, .json, or .csv structure files on disk. The badge at index.html:42 that reads "AlphaFold Server Live Connected" is a static anchor tag; nothing is connected and nothing is live. The only "integration" is app.js:660-671, which copies a string to the clipboard for a human to paste manually into a browser. Consequence: The platform's single central claim -- README.md:22, "models 25 De Novo Targeted Bio-Conjugate Therapeutics designed via AlphaFold3" -- is false as a statement about this software. A reviewer, collaborator, funder, or acquirer who reads the README and the UI will believe structure prediction was performed; opening app.js reveals it was not. Every downstream artifact (the leaderboard, the 25 drug cards, the confidence plots) inherits this and is therefore unusable as evidence for anything. This is a provenance failure rather than an accuracy failure, which is worse: accuracy failures can be measured and corrected, provenance failures destroy trust in the entire artifact.

text: [BLOCKER] All pLDDT and PAE values are closed-form fakes that are statistically distinguishable from real AlphaFold3 output — The pLDDT curve is `93 + Math.sin(i*0.4)*4 + (char.charCodeAt(0) % 5)*0.5` (app.js:791). Over the 20 standard amino acids ord(aa)%5 spans 0..4, so the expression is analytically bounded to [93-4+0.0, 93+4+2.0] = [89.0, 99.0]. I reproduced the generator over all 25 drug sequences (876 residues): observed min 89.0, max 99.0, mean 94.11, and 0.0% of residues below 70. Consequences: (i) the clamps at app.js:792-793 are unreachable dead code; (ii) the legend at index.html:390-391 advertises "Low (50-70)" and "Very Low (<50)" bands that can never be produced; (iii) there is no terminal droop -- the mean value at residue 1 is 95.50, *higher* than the global mean of 94.11, whereas real AF3 termini drop sharply; (iv) flexible linkers are invisible. HippoDual-TrkB-AMPK-X5 (app.js:183) has a GGGGS linker at index 9 and the generator returns [90.5, 89.7, 89.5, 90.0, 92.0] there; CogDual-TrkB-PAS-10 (app.js:125) has a 15-residue (GGGGS)x3 linker at indices 49-63 and the generator returns ~96-97. Real AF3 puts a Gly-Ser linker at pLDDT 30-60. The PAE matrix is `Math.abs(i-j)*0.4 + (sequence.charCodeAt(i % len) % 4)*0.3` (app.js:850). Subtracting the 0.4|i-j| ramp leaves a residual that takes exactly four discrete values {0.0, 0.3, 0.6, 0.9} and depends only on the row index i -- the matrix is exactly PAE = 0.4|i-j| + f(i). There are no domain blocks, no inter-chain block, and no contact structure. For a 45-residue chain the analytic maximum is 44*0.4+0.9 = 18.50 A, so the 30 A clamp at app.js:851 is dead code and the "0 - 30 Å" range advertised at index.html:397 and README.md:110 is never reached. Separately, app.js:844 caps the grid at `Math.min(len, 45)`, silently dropping residues 46-47 of HippoTrk-Saponin-X1 (47 aa) with no indication in the UI. Finally, the two fabrications disagree with each other: the modal prints "AF3 pLDDT = 97.0 / 100" for HippoNrf-KeapDecoy-X3 (app.js:166) while the chart rendered in the same popup has mean 94.31 (delta -2.69); deltas across the 25 drugs range from -2.69 to +1.69 in both directions. Consequence: These plots carry the labels "AlphaFold3 pLDDT Score" (app.js:802), "AlphaFold3 Real Sequence-Driven 3D Model & PAE Heatmap Graphs" (index.html:371), and "Predicted Aligned Error 2D domain contact heatmap (0 - 30 Å)" (README.md:110). Any structural biologist reading them will interpret them as model output and will conclude the designs are uniformly high-confidence, well-ordered, single-domain constructs. All three conclusions are artifacts of the formula. The most damaging consequence is the inverted signal at the linkers: the (GGGGS)x3 spacers are the one part of these constructs where a real prediction would flag low confidence and a bright inter-domain PAE block, i.e. the exact information a designer needs to decide whether a bispecific construct will hold its two warheads in a defined relative orientation. The fake reports the opposite. The internal disagreement between the chart mean and the printed pLDDT string is a self-contained proof of fabrication that requires no external ground truth to establish.

text: Ground truth for AIML-02: Real AF3 pLDDT is a per-atom predicted lDDT on a 0-100 scale, written to `atom_plddts` in confidences.json (google-deepmind/alphafold3 docs/output.md). Empirically it has a characteristic signature: sharp droop over the first and last few residues, dips to 40-70 in loops and flexible linkers, near-90+ plateaus in secondary-structure elements, and values below 50 in genuinely disordered segments -- AF3 additionally reports `fraction_disordered` for exactly this reason. Real PAE (Abramson et al., Nature 630:493-500, 2024, DOI 10.1038/s41586-024-07487-w) is a token x token estimate of the error in relative position and orientation between two tokens; for multi-domain or multi-chain systems it is visibly block-structured, with low intra-unit blocks (typically <5 A) and high off-diagonal cross-unit blocks (10-30 A) separated by sharp edges. It does not increase linearly with sequence separation, and its asymmetry reflects the choice of alignment frame, not a per-row constant.

text: [CRITICAL] pLDDT is misused as a binder-quality and affinity metric; the interface metrics that actually govern binder design (ipTM, interface PAE, ranking_score) are absent — Three distinct errors are compounded. (1) pLDDT is presented as a design-quality score. It is not. pLDDT is the model's prediction of its own lDDT -- a self-consistency estimate of *local* geometric confidence. It measures neither correctness nor binding. A high pLDDT means the model would reproduce its own local environment under superposition; it says nothing about whether the peptide binds the named receptor, or binds anything. (2) pLDDT is packed into the same string as a dG in kcal/mol and a Kd in nM (app.js:146 and 24 others), implying they are commensurate outputs of one calculation. AF3 emits no free energy and no dissociation constant, and no combination of its outputs can be converted into one. The dG/Kd pairs are also internally inconsistent with each other: applying dG = RT ln(Kd) at 298.15 K (RT = 0.5925 kcal/mol), dG = -18.4 implies Kd = 0.033 pM, but the table states 0.32 nM -- a factor of ~9,800. Across all 25 drugs the stated Kd values are on average 10^3.47 too high, and a regression of log10(Kd) on dG gives r = 0.9969 with an implied RT of 1.056 kcal/mol, i.e. an implied temperature of 531 K. The numbers were produced by a wrong constant, not by a thermodynamic calculation. (3) The ranking is not what it claims. The tab is titled "AlphaFold3 Leaderboard Ranking" (index.html:296) but Spearman(rank, pLDDT) = -0.612 while Spearman(rank, CEI) = -0.988. The leaderboard is actually sorted by "CEI", a "Cognitive Enhancement Index" that appears only as a chart label (app.js:1063) and a column header (index.html:306) and is defined nowhere in the repository. Meanwhile ipTM, pTM, ranking_score, has_clash, and chain_pair_pae_min -- the metrics AF3 actually provides for judging an interface -- appear zero times. Consequence: This is the error that would most mislead a domain expert, because it is stated in fluent, correct-sounding vocabulary. A reader is invited to believe that pLDDT 96.2 means "this binder is better" and that pLDDT and dG are two views of one prediction. Neither is true, and acting on that belief is how binder-design campaigns fail: designed sequences are precisely the regime where AF confidence is least trustworthy, because idealized de novo sequences fold cleanly and confidently in the model whether or not they engage the target. Filtering or ranking designs on monomer pLDDT selects for designability, not for binding, and will pass through a set of well-folded non-binders at essentially the base rate. The field settled this question a decade into the deep-learning era and the answer is well documented.

text: Required fix for AIML-03: Remove pLDDT from any ranking or quality role. Rank candidates on ipTM and interface PAE computed from a real prediction of the *complex* (binder chain + receptor chain), with ranking_score as the tiebreak, and display has_clash as a hard filter. Split the `affinity:` strings so that model confidence and thermodynamic quantities are never presented in the same field, and remove all dG and Kd values unless they are produced by an actual free-energy method (FEP/TI, MM-GBSA with a stated protocol, or an affinity-predicting model such as Boltz-2, which emits log10(IC50 in µM) rather than a kcal/mol dG) with the method, force field, and error bars cited. Either define CEI explicitly with its formula and inputs, or delete the column and the chart series; and rename index.html:296 to reflect whatever metric actually determines the sort order.

tags: Machine learning for protein structure prediction (AlphaFold-class models): model outputs, confidence calibration, de novo binder design evaluation, and inference infrastructure
text: Ground truth for AIML-03: AF3's actual confidence outputs (Abramson et al., Nature 630:493-500, 2024, DOI 10.1038/s41586-024-07487-w; google-deepmind/alphafold3 docs/output.md) are: per-atom pLDDT (0-100, `atom_plddts`) = local geometric confidence, does NOT measure global topology, inter-chain placement, or binding; PAE (token x token, in Å, `pae`) = expected error in the relative position/orientation of two tokens, the correct metric for domain and chain placement; pTM (0-1) = predicted TM-score of the whole complex, >0.5 means the overall fold may be right; ipTM (0-1) = predicted accuracy of the *relative placement of subunits*, the interface metric, with >0.8 confident, <0.6 a likely failure and 0.6-0.8 a gray zone; ranking_score (range [-100, 1.5]) = AF3's own model-selection score; plus has_clash, fraction_disordered, chain_pair_iptm, and chain_pair_pae_min. None of these is a binding free energy or a Kd. For designed binders specifically, Bennett et al. (Nat Commun 14:2625, 2023, PMID 37149653, DOI 10.1038/s41467-023-38328-5) established that filtering with AlphaFold2's interface predicted-aligned-error (pAE_interaction) -- not monomer pLDDT -- raises experimental binder success rates roughly ten-fold. Karelina, Noh & Dror (eLife 12:RP89386, 2023) showed independently that high-confidence AlphaFold models do not translate into accurate ligand poses, reinforcing that model confidence and binding accuracy are separate axes.

text: [CRITICAL] The "REAL FASTA SEQUENCE PARSING & 3D BACKBONE TOPOLOGY" viewer renders a physically impossible helix whose geometry is set by ASCII codes, and its "pLDDT color spectrum" is keyed on residue letter, not confidence — The comment at app.js:707 claims "REAL FASTA SEQUENCE PARSING & 3D BACKBONE TOPOLOGY GENERATION" and index.html:377 labels the panel "Real Sequence 3D Structure (pLDDT Color Spectrum)". The code does neither. Geometry: helix radius = `6 + (charCode % 5) * 0.8` (app.js:715), i.e. 6.0-9.2 units, multiplied by 1.3 for Cys and Pro (app.js:723-727) up to 12.0; rise = 0.6 per residue; and the total turn count is `(i/seqLength) * PI * (charCode%3===0 ? 6 : 4)` (app.js:717), which fixes the number of turns at 2 or 3 regardless of chain length, so the pitch scales with length -- the inverse of how a real helix behaves. I measured the resulting virtual bond lengths: for HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 (36 aa) consecutive point spacing runs 1.21 to 15.77 (mean 6.41); for HippoNrf-KeapDecoy-X3 (28 aa) it runs 0.63 to 16.63 (mean 7.90). A real trans-peptide Ca(i)-Ca(i+1) distance is 3.80 +/- 0.04 A and is essentially invariant; a 15.8 A virtual bond is over four peptide bonds' worth of separation and a 0.63 A one is a steric impossibility. A real alpha-helix has radius 2.3 A, rise 1.5 A per residue, and 3.6 residues per turn -- none of which this reproduces. The determining variable throughout is `charCode % 5`, the ASCII code of the letter modulo 5, a quantity with no chemical meaning whatsoever (it makes Ala and Phe identical and Cys and Trp identical). Coloring: app.js:747-749 assigns cyan by default, green if the residue is G or S, and amber if it is P or D. The comments on those very lines read "// Very High (>90)", "// High", "// Low" -- so residue identity is being presented to the user as a confidence band. The code never reads any pLDDT value, and it directly contradicts the chart generated in the same modal at app.js:791, which places 92.4% of those same residues above 90 and would therefore color them all cyan. Binding site: app.js:757-761 (and app.js:1012-1021) place a fixed-radius wireframe sphere at the origin, identical for all 25 drugs and all 10 candidates, unrelated to any of the `bindingSites` residue strings. Consequence: This is the panel a viewer will trust most, because 3D structure reads as ground truth in a way a line chart does not, and it sits directly under a heading containing the words "Real" and "AlphaFold3". A user will believe they are looking at a predicted fold of the named construct, colored by predicted confidence, with a marked binding pocket. They are looking at none of those things: they are looking at the same helix 25 times, tinted by which letters happen to appear in the string, with a decorative sphere at the origin. Because the coloring is keyed on letter identity, Gly/Ser-rich linkers -- which really are low-confidence -- are colored "High" green while Pro and Asp anywhere in the chain, including in well-ordered turns, are colored "Low" amber. The visual is not merely uninformative; it points the reader's attention at the wrong residues.

Backbone geometry is determined by the predicted Cartesian coordinates in the model .cif: Ca-Ca 3.80 +/- 0.04 A for trans peptides (~2.9 A for the rare cis-Pro), alpha-helix radius 2.3 A with 1.5 A rise and 3.6 residues/turn, beta-strand rise 3.3-3.4 A per residue. pLDDT coloring uses the per-atom `atom_plddts` array from confidences.json against the standard AlphaFold bands (>90 very high / 70-90 confident / 50-70 low / <50 very low). Binding-site annotation comes from the predicted complex -- residues within a distance cutoff of the partner chain or ligand -- not from a fixed sphere at the coordinate origin.

text: [CRITICAL] The claimed AlphaFold3 jobs are under-specified: no receptor chain and no ligand entity, so no reported quantity is obtainable even from a genuine AF3 run — Every one of the 25 therapeutics and 10 leaderboard candidates is described as a bio-conjugate of a natural-product warhead fused to a targeting peptide -- app.js:142 is explicit: "Ginsenoside Rg1 Dammarane-12,20-diol (C42H72O14) + C-20 Linker". But the only thing carried in the data structure and the only thing fed to the viewer, the pLDDT chart, and the PAE heatmap (app.js:648-652) is the bare peptide string. The small molecule is never expressed as a SMILES string or a CCD code, and there is no ligand entity of any kind. Equally important, the *target receptor* is never included either: `bindingSites` names TrkB D5 residues Asp298/Glu319/Tyr342/Val312/Leu333 (app.js:144) as free text, but no TrkB sequence, no UniProt accession, and no receptor chain appears anywhere. The claimed AF3 job is therefore a single unbound peptide in vacuum. Such a job cannot produce a binding site, an interface, an ipTM, an inter-chain PAE block, a dG, or a Kd -- these quantities are undefined for a monomer. This is not a matter of the numbers being wrong; the numbers are not computable from the stated input. It is also a straight inversion of AF3's actual contribution: joint prediction of protein-ligand and protein-protein complexes is the entire reason AF3 exists over AF2, and this platform uses none of it. Consequence: A reader who accepts the framing will believe that AF3 was asked "does this conjugate bind TrkB D5, and how well?" and answered. The question was never posed. Any decision made downstream -- which of the 25 to synthesize, which region to prioritize, whether the bispecific designs hold their two warheads in a defined geometry -- rests on an input specification that could not have addressed it. For the bispecific candidates in particular (X5, P5, B5, M5, A5, and CogDual-TrkB-PAS-10) the entire design question is the relative orientation of two binding modules across a linker, which is an inter-domain PAE / ipTM question about a complex. A monomer job is structurally incapable of answering it.

text: Required fix for AIML-05: Redefine each candidate as a complete AF3 job specification rather than a bare string: a `target` field carrying the receptor UniProt accession and the exact domain sequence used, a `binder` field for the designed peptide, and a `ligand` field carrying the warhead as SMILES or CCD plus the covalent bond specification to the conjugation residue. Run prediction on the complex. Report ipTM, chain_pair_pae_min, has_clash, and the interface PAE block, and drop dG/Kd unless separately computed by a named free-energy method with stated error bars.

tags: Machine learning for protein structure prediction (AlphaFold-class models): model outputs, confidence calibration, de novo binder design evaluation, and inference infrastructure
text: Ground truth for AIML-05: An AF3 input JSON specifies a list of `sequences` entities: `proteinChain` (with sequence and copy count), `ligand` (by CCD code or SMILES), `dna`/`rna`, plus optional bonded-atom pairs for covalent conjugates, ions, and post-translational modifications (google-deepmind/alphafold3, input/output docs, retrieved this session). To evaluate a peptide-conjugate binder against TrkB you must supply at minimum: the TrkB D5 domain chain (UniProt Q16620, the Ig-like C2-type 2 domain), the designed peptide chain, and the natural-product warhead as a ligand entity with an explicit covalent linkage to the peptide. Only then does AF3 report `iptm`, `chain_pair_iptm`, `chain_pair_pae_min`, and a cross-chain PAE block -- the quantities that actually speak to binding. Absolute binding free energy is not an AF3 output at all and requires a separate method (alchemical FEP/TI, MM-GB/PBSA with a stated protocol, or an affinity model such as Boltz-2).

text: [MAJOR] Two sequences contain the non-residue character 'B' and one field is not a sequence at all, yet all three are fed to the pLDDT, PAE, and 3D generators without validation — I scanned all 25 modal sequences and all 10 leaderboard FASTA strings against the 20 standard one-letter codes. Three entries fail. 'B' appears at index 18 in app.js:173, app.js:371, and app.js:130; B is the IUPAC ambiguity code for Asx (Asn or Asp), not a residue, and is not an acceptable character in an AF3 `proteinChain` sequence. More seriously, app.js:381 sets `sequence: "His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate"` -- a prose description, not a sequence. The application does not validate any of these. It passes the prose string straight into initModal3DCanvas, renderModalPlddtChart, and renderModalPaeHeatmap, which treat it as a 37-residue chain and generate a complete "AlphaFold3 pLDDT Score" curve, a PAE heatmap, and a 3D backbone from the ASCII codes of its lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens. The UI labels the result identically to the other 24. The modal for A4 additionally prints "AF3 pLDDT = 92.4 / 100" (app.js:384) for this non-sequence. There is no input validation anywhere in the codebase and no error path. Consequence: This is the cleanest available proof that no prediction ever ran: a real pipeline would have failed loudly on 'B' at the parser and could not have accepted "His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate" at all. It also means the "Copy FASTA Sequence" button (app.js:660-671) hands users strings that will be rejected by AlphaFold Server, by any AF3-class local model, and by most FASTA tooling -- so the one manual workflow the app does support is broken for three of its entries. And because A4's fake curve is indistinguishable from the other 24, a user has no way to tell that one card is describing nothing at all.

text: [MAJOR] AlphaFold3 availability is misrepresented, the described workflow is prohibited by the AlphaFold Server terms, and DeepMind affiliation is implied — The project presents AlphaFold3 as a freely available service it is plugged into, and presents itself as associated with DeepMind. Neither is accurate. On availability: the AF3 source at github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3 is Apache 2.0, but the code is inert without model parameters, and the parameters are governed by a separate AlphaFold 3 Model Parameters Terms of Use under which access is granted only to non-commercial organizations on request directly from Google, weights "must not" be published or shared outside the receiving organization, and use "in connection with any commercial activities, including research on behalf of commercial organizations" is forbidden. On the server route: AlphaFold Server is non-commercial-only, is subject to a daily job quota (launched at 10 requests/day, later raised to 20), exposes no API, supports only a restricted CCD-based ligand set rather than arbitrary SMILES, and its Prohibited Use Policy states that users must not use AlphaFold Server or its outputs "in connection with any automated system that predicts the binding or interaction of the protein with ligands or peptides, including, but not limited to, Glide or AutoDock." A platform whose stated purpose (README.md:22) is automated de novo bio-conjugate binder design against named receptors is squarely inside that prohibition. On affiliation: the shields.io badge at README.md:3 reads "AlphaFold3 | DeepMind_Server" with a Google logo, the page subtitle at index.html:30 reads "DeepMind Structural Pharmacology & AlphaFold3 De Novo Platform", the footer at index.html:410 reads "Generated with AlphaFold3 3D Structural Modeling", and the repository lives in a directory named DeepMind_Bio. Nothing in the project is from, endorsed by, or connected to Google DeepMind. Consequence: Three separate exposures. Scientifically, a reader is led to believe local automated AF3 inference at scale is a routine thing this project does, which sets a false expectation about how reproducible the work is -- nobody can rerun it, and not only because there is no code. Legally, if any commercial use is contemplated, the described workflow is not merely unimplemented but not permitted by the route named, and the Google-branded badge plus "DeepMind" in the product subtitle and the repo path constitutes an implied endorsement that is not authorized. Practically, it obscures the fact that a fully permissive path exists and is what a real build should use.

text: Required fix for AIML-07: Remove the DeepMind/Google-branded badge at README.md:3, remove "DeepMind" from the subtitle at index.html:30, remove the "Generated with AlphaFold3" footer at index.html:410, and rename the project directory away from DeepMind_Bio. Replace the claimed AF3 dependency with one of the permissively licensed models above -- Boltz-2 or Chai-1 are the closest fit here, since both can be run locally in an automated pipeline and Boltz-2 additionally emits an affinity estimate to replace the fabricated dG/Kd column -- and state the chosen model, its version, and its license in the README. If AF3 itself is genuinely wanted, add an explicit statement that weights must be requested from Google under non-commercial terms and that the AlphaFold Server route may not be used for automated binding prediction.

text: Ground truth for AIML-07: AlphaFold 3: code Apache 2.0 (github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/LICENSE); model parameters under the separate AlphaFold 3 Model Parameters Terms of Use -- request-only, non-commercial organizations only, no redistribution outside the receiving organization, outputs may be published but may not be used to train competing structure-prediction models. Permissively licensed AF3-class models that DO allow local automated and commercial inference: Boltz-1 and Boltz-2 (MIT, code and weights; Boltz-2 additionally predicts binding affinity as log10(IC50 in µM)); Chai-1 (Apache 2.0, code and weights, explicitly usable for drug discovery); Protenix (Apache 2.0, free for academic and commercial use); OpenFold3 (Apache 2.0, a reproduction of AF3 from the AlQuraishi Lab / OpenFold consortium, academic and commercial use).

text: [MINOR] Modal WebGL contexts and animation loops leak on every drug-card open, multiplying render calls and rotation speed — Each time a drug card is opened, initModal3DCanvas creates a fresh THREE.WebGLRenderer (app.js:688) and starts a new animateModal3D requestAnimationFrame loop (app.js:772). The previous renderer's canvas is discarded by `container.innerHTML = ''` (app.js:678) but `.dispose()` is never called, so its WebGL context is never released; likewise the previous geometries, materials, and textures are never disposed. Worse, the guard at app.js:764 is `if (!modalThreeRenderer) return;` against a module-scope variable that has just been *reassigned* to the new renderer -- so the stale loop does not exit. It sees the new renderer as truthy, applies `modalThreeMeshGroup.rotation.y += 0.006` to the *new* group, and calls render on the *new* scene. After k modal opens, k loops are alive, the model spins at k*0.006 rad/frame, and the scene is rendered k times per frame. closeDrugModal (app.js:655-658) only toggles a CSS class and cancels nothing. Consequence: Browsers cap live WebGL contexts (typically ~16 in Chrome); past that the oldest are force-lost and the viewer goes blank or throws. Since the platform's headline interaction is browsing 25 drug cards, a user doing exactly what the UI invites will hit the cap partway through and see the 3D panel fail, with visibly accelerating rotation beforehand. This is a real defect independent of the scientific issues, and it would persist verbatim after a correct viewer is wired in -- so it is worth fixing as part of that work rather than after.

text: Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3 (2024). The primary AlphaFold3 paper. Defines the model's confidence outputs and their semantics: pLDDT (per-atom predicted lDDT, 0-100, local geometric confidence), PAE (token x token estimate of error in the relative position and orientation of two tokens, in Angstroms), pTM (0-1, predicted TM-score of the whole complex; >0.5 suggests the overall fold may be correct), and ipTM (0-1, accuracy of the relative placement of subunits; >0.8 confident, <0.6 likely failed, 0.6-0.8 a gray zone). Establishes that AF3 jointly predicts protein-ligand, protein-nucleic-acid, and protein-protein complexes -- the capability this platform names but never uses. Application here: This is the ground truth against which every metric claim in the repository should be rewritten. Use it to justify replacing the pLDDT-based ranking (index.html:296-306, app.js:124-135) with ipTM plus interface PAE, and to justify deleting the dG/Kd fields (app.js:146 and 24 others) since AF3 outputs neither. The ipTM thresholds (>0.8 / 0.6-0.8 / <0.6) give the platform a defensible confidence banding to replace the fabricated one.

text: AlphaFold 3 output specification (docs/output.md) and Model Parameters Terms of Use (WEIGHTS_TERMS_OF_USE.md) (2024). The exact output contract: per job, `<name>_model.cif`, `<name>_confidences.json` (containing `pae`, `atom_plddts`, `contact_probs`, `token_chain_ids`, `atom_chain_ids`), `<name>_summary_confidences.json` (containing `ptm`, `iptm`, `ranking_score` in [-100, 1.5], `fraction_disordered`, `has_clash`, `chain_pair_pae_min`, `chain_pair_iptm`, `chain_ptm`, `chain_iptm`), `<name>_data.json`, and `ranking_scores.csv`. Confirms pLDDT in AF3 is per-atom, not per-residue. The LICENSE is Apache 2.0 for code; the weights are governed by separate terms restricting access to non-commercial organizations on request from Google, forbidding redistribution outside the receiving organization and any commercial use. Application here: Provides the exact absence proof for finding AIML-01 (none of these filenames or field names appear in the repository) and the file schema a real backend must parse for AIML-02 and AIML-04. The weights terms are the legal basis for AIML-07 and for recommending a permissively licensed alternative instead.

tags: Machine learning for protein structure prediction (AlphaFold-class models): model outputs, confidence calibration, de novo binder design evaluation, and inference infrastructure
text: Improving de novo protein binder design with deep learning (2023). Bennett, Coventry, Goreshnik, Huang, Allen, Vafeados, Peng, Dauparas, Baek, Stewart, DiMaio, De Munck, Savvides, Baker. Establishes the standard evaluation protocol for de novo binder design: filtering candidates with AlphaFold2's interface predicted-aligned-error (pAE_interaction) rather than monomer confidence raises experimental success rates roughly ten-fold, and ProteinMPNN sequence design substantially improves efficiency over Rosetta. Documents realistic experimental hit rates for designed binders (single-digit percent even with good in silico filters). Application here: Directly supports AIML-03: this is the field-standard evidence that interface PAE, not pLDDT, is the operative filter for designed binders. Also calibrates expectations -- the platform implies 25 of 25 designs succeed with sub-nanomolar Kd, whereas the literature baseline for AF-filtered de novo binders is a few percent hit rate. Any honest rewrite should adopt interface-PAE/ipTM filtering and report a candidate pool rather than 25 guaranteed successes.

tags: Machine learning for protein structure prediction (AlphaFold-class models): model outputs, confidence calibration, de novo binder design evaluation, and inference infrastructure
text: How accurately can one predict drug binding modes using AlphaFold models? (2023). A rigorous assessment on GPCRs showing that ligand poses docked into AlphaFold2 models are not significantly more accurate than poses from traditional template-based homology models, and are much less accurate than poses docked into experimental structures -- even though the AF2 binding pockets themselves are near-experimental in accuracy. Demonstrates that high model confidence does not translate into accurate ligand placement. Application here: Supports AIML-03 and AIML-05: model confidence and binding accuracy are orthogonal axes. Cite this to justify removing any claim that a confident structure prediction implies a validated binding mode or a computable affinity for the natural-product warheads described at app.js:142 and throughout FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA.

text: Boltz-1: Democratizing Biomolecular Interaction Modeling; and Boltz-2: Towards Accurate and Efficient Binding Affinity Prediction (2025). Open AF3-class biomolecular structure prediction under the MIT license for both code and weights, explicitly free for academic and commercial use. Boltz-2 additionally predicts binding affinity, reporting `affinity_pred_value` as log10(IC50) with IC50 in µM plus `affinity_probability_binary` in [0,1] for binder/non-binder discrimination. Application here: The single best replacement for the fictional AF3 backend. Boltz-2 can be run locally and automated without licensing conflict (unlike AF3 weights or AlphaFold Server), it emits the real confidence fields needed to fix AIML-02 and AIML-03, and its affinity head gives a legitimate, citable quantity to put in place of the fabricated dG/Kd column -- reported in its native log10(IC50 µM) units, not converted into a spurious kcal/mol free energy.

tags: Machine learning for protein structure prediction (AlphaFold-class models): model outputs, confidence calibration, de novo binder design evaluation, and inference infrastructure
text: Chai-1: Decoding the molecular interactions of life (2024). An AF3-class multimodal structure prediction model released under Apache 2.0 for both code and model weights, explicitly permitted for academic and commercial use including drug discovery. Supports protein, ligand, nucleic acid, and covalent-modification entities in a single job. Application here: A second viable local backend, and the one to prefer if a permissive license covering weights as well as code is a hard requirement. Its job specification is the template for fixing AIML-05: supply the receptor chain, the designed peptide chain, and the natural-product warhead as an explicit ligand entity with a covalent bond, rather than a bare peptide string.

tags: Machine learning for protein structure prediction (AlphaFold-class models): model outputs, confidence calibration, de novo binder design evaluation, and inference infrastructure
text: Protenix (ByteDance) and OpenFold3 (AlQuraishi Lab / OpenFold consortium) (2025). Two further open AF3 reproductions, both Apache 2.0 and free for academic and commercial use. Protenix reports outperforming AlphaFold3 across benchmark sets at matched training-data cutoff, model scale, and inference budget. OpenFold3 aims at a bitwise reproduction of AlphaFold3 and ships full training data and a trainable framework, making it the option to choose if fine-tuning on a proprietary binder set is ever wanted. Application here: Completes the set of legally usable backends for AIML-07 and demonstrates concretely that the licensing obstacle the project implicitly works around does not require working around -- a fully open, commercially usable AF3-class model can be installed and run locally today. OpenFold3's trainability is the relevant option if the project later wants a model tuned on CNS peptide binders.
